messages:
maria: heads-up — nightly perf dashboard just flagged a sharp tail-latency increase around 02:10 UTC. p95 up ~120ms on the batching workload compared to baseline :eyes:
ben: link?
ryan: grabbing it now, can you paste the alert snapshot?
maria: https://dash.internal/redwood/nightly/perf?panel=p95_batching — look at the spike at ~02:08, throughput steady.
ben: interestingly p50 unchanged, so this smells like kernel selection or a cold-KV path.
tao: I pulled a quick flamegraph from the canary: heavy time in kernel_selector::choose_fp_path() and then a fallback into slow_fp_kernel.
jen: who pushed to main last night? any merge windows?
ci-bot: merge 0a9f3b -> main by ryan at 01:54 UTC (quantize: prefer-policy change). CI perf checks passed (non-blocking).
ryan: that quantize prefer-policy change was supposed to prefer int8 kernels for tiny sequences — maybe selector logic flipped for medium sequences too.
maria: timeline aligns: spike appears ~15m after the merge, which is when overnight traffic rolled onto the new image.
ben: quick repro on staging w/ workload generator:
```
./bin/loadtest --model=redwood-v2-small --seq=128 --qps=120 --duration=600
```
results: tail latency jumps when we enable the new quantize policy.
ta o: (edited) typo: tao here — did a local diff; kernel_selector now uses a policy severity threshold variable instead of a hard cutoff. That variable default changed in the merge.
jen: can we bisect the change? If it's the variable default it's an easy revert or config fix.
ryan: starting git bisect against the pipeline image list. will report back.
ci-bot: running perf microbench on images (automated) — will post summaries.
ben: meanwhile, is KV cache eviction rate higher? any cold starts?
sre-bot: infra note: no instance churn during spike window, nodes stayed up. KV miss rate increased 2.2x for affected route.
maria: ok that points at a path where selector chooses a kernel that doesn't reuse KV cache layout well.
ryan: bisect found the suspect commit: 0a9f3b2 changed policy_threshold from 0.7 -> 0.4 and added a fallback probe that prefers non-quantized kernel when probe fails. Probe failure rate is ~3% on warm caches -> causes slow path for those requests.
tao: probe code:```cpp
bool probe_kernel() {
  if (!kv_cache.warmed()) return false; // new check
  return try_fast_quantized();
}
```
ben: so small fraction of requests see kv_cache.warmed() == false and go slow. With continuous batching, those propagate and spike tail.
jen: mitigation options: revert commit, or change probe to check recent success rate instead of warm flag. Which is low-risk?
ryan: quick patch candidate: set policy_threshold back to 0.7 and disable the new kv warm gate. I'll run a canary build.
ci-bot: canary build queued: image=canary-quant-fix-612999. Perf tests scheduled.
ben: if canary looks good we should hold rollout and revert the merge on main.
maria: canary perf graph posted: p95 back to baseline, kv miss rate normalized. :thumbsup:
jen: please open a revert PR and mark rollout hold. I'll message product.
ryan: revert PR #4987 opened, adding changelog and postmortem note.
ta o: adding a follow-up issue to replace boolean warm gate with sliding-window probe success metric.
sre-bot: rollout hold applied to main at 03:05 UTC.
ci-bot: CI perf regression alert cleared after revert branch deployed to nightly.
ben: postmortem quick notes: cause = policy_threshold change + new kv_warmed gate -> <3% probe failures -> kernel selector fallback to slow FP kernel -> p95 spike. Remediation = revert + design fix.
maria: thanks all — we'll track the design ticket (ENG-1523) and schedule a deeper perf test for different seq lengths. Closing triage for now :white_check_mark:
